messages:
Marta R.: Heads up — CloudHub reported a ~2% mismatch between our hourly invoice rolls and their hourly telemetry this morning. looks like drift around the 03:00-04:00 window.
Sam K.: ugh, again. is this the timezone/daylight-savings thing or something else? :grimacing:
Marta R.: not DST. the pattern: partner sent minute-level events, we bucket into hourly rolls, but some events land in the previous hour on their side. suspecting differing boundary rules + TTLs on their agent replay.
Laura (PM): can we get a minimal repro? CloudHub says they saw 00:59:xx events with seq_id that we later attribute to 01:00 on our side.
Ethan S.: possible cause: partner is shipping events with an event_ts and a processed_ts. our ingestion uses processed_ts for bucket assignment when event_ts is missing/older than X mins. if their agent batches/retains, processed_ts can jump and shift hour.
Marta R.: I captured an example payload from CloudHub. sharing sanitized snippet:
```
{
  "event_id": "ch-8992",
  "seq_id": 12345678,
  "event_ts": "2025-07-14T00:59:41Z",
  "processed_ts": "2025-07-14T01:00:03Z",
  "usage_units": 1
}
```
Marta R.: they expect attribution by event_ts. we currently prefer processed_ts if event_ts < ingestion_cutoff (30m). their replay behavior causes processed_ts to cross the hour boundary.
Sam K.: Ok — quick options:
1) change attribution to always use event_ts if present (simplest for partners that include it)
2) make the ingestion_cutoff configurable per-partner (safer)
3) emit a reconciliation delta metric and run daily backfill for hour boundaries
Sam K.: Thoughts on production risk?
Ethan S.: 1 is easy but risky if partners send bad event_ts (clock skew). 2 is ok — we already support partner-specific ingestion configs but never surfaced this boundary. 3 is operational overhead.
Laura (PM): partner asks for SLA-friendly behavior. propose: default to event_ts if event_ts exists AND seq_id is present, else fallback to processed_ts. seq_id gives us monotonicity to detect bad clocks.
Marta R.: I like that. adds minimal change and aligns with partner expectation. we'll also log a mismatch metric when event_ts and processed_ts cross hour boundary for 7 days.
metering-bot: New alert rule created: partner.hourly.drift.alert (severity: low) — triggers on >0.5% hourly delta for two consecutive hours.
Sam K.: action items:
- Ethan: implement fallback logic (event_ts + seq_id check) in ingestion (ETA Tue EOD) — create PR
- Marta: coordinate with CloudHub to confirm seq_id semantics and share test payloads (ETA Mon)
- Laura: update partner-facing doc and add config toggle to partner portal (ETA Wed)
Marta R.: I'll also add a quick smoke test: `curl -X POST https://ingest.redwood.example/partners/cloudhub/test -d @sample.json` and validate hour buckets in the test dashboard.
Ethan S.: noted. I'll add unit tests for edgecases: seq_id reset, negative clock skew > 24h, and large batch replays.
Laura (PM): can we add a one-off backfill job to reconcile the last 72h after change goes live? CloudHub wants historical correction too.
Sam K.: yes — create a small mapreduce job that reassigns events based on event_ts where seq_id present. low risk; run in canary first.
Marta R.: Thanks all. I'll ping once CloudHub confirms seq_id guarantee. tagging @CloudHub (external) in the follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
metering-bot: Ticket created: PARTNERS-2148 — "CloudHub hourly attribution drift / seq_id handshake" assigned to Ethan S., Marta R., Laura (PM).
